name: Construction retainage limits by US state — maximum withholding percentages, release deadlines, escrow requirements, and public vs private distinctions with statutory citations
description: State-by-state comparison of the statutory rules governing retainage (retention) on construction contracts. Each record is one state with the maximum retainage percentage for public and private projects, the deadline for releasing retained funds after substantial completion, whether retainage must be held in an interest-bearing escrow account, whether the cap is reduced after a completion milestone (e.g. 50% complete), and the statutory citation. Caps range from 0% (New Mexico) to 10%, with a strong trend toward 5%. Answers 'how much retainage can be withheld on my project in [state]', 'when must retainage be released', and 'does my state require retainage escrow'.

records.public_cap_pct: 10%; 5% after the contract is 50% complete; no retention at all for job-order-contracting contracts
records.private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in this section, which governs retention by the state
records.release_deadline: within sixty days after final completion and acceptance
records.escrow_required: no (the contractor may provide substitute security instead, and keeps the interest)
records.milestone_reduction: at 50% complete, one-half of the amount retained is released and later retention is capped at five per cent
records.source_quote: A. Ten per cent of all construction contract payments shall be retained by this state as insurance of proper performance of the contract or, at the option of the contractor, a substitute security may be provided by the contractor in an authorized form pursuant to rules adopted by the director.

records.release_deadline: upon final completion and acceptance of the project
records.milestone_reduction: after 95% of the work has been completed, the department may reduce the funds withheld to an amount not less than 125 percent of the estimated value of the work yet to be completed
records.source_quote: The department shall withhold not more than 5 percent of the contract price until final completion and acceptance of the project. However, at any time after 95 percent of the work has been completed, the department may reduce the funds withheld to an amount not less than 125 percent of the estimated value of the work yet to be completed

records.release_deadline: not specified in this section
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: A property owner, contractor, or subcontractor shall not withhold as retainage more than five percent of the price of the work completed under the contract or subcontract.

records.public_cap_pct: 7.5% on a state agency contract, reduced to five per cent when fifty per cent of the contract is completed; 2.5% on a Department of Transportation contract; 5% where the awarding authority is a municipality
records.private_cap_pct: five per cent of the estimated amount of a progress payment for the life of the construction project
records.release_deadline: not later than thirty days after the issuance of a certificate of final completion by the owner or the owner's authorized representative, or thirty days after the owner's equivalent written acceptance of the work (private work); § 49-41b sets no final-release deadline for public work
records.escrow_required: yes on private work — an escrow account shall be established for all retainage, in a state or national bank or a savings and loan domiciled in this state; § 42-158q keeps that duty off any public building or public work of the state or a municipality, so none on public work
records.milestone_reduction: on a state agency contract the seven and one-half per cent drops to five per cent when fifty per cent of the contract is completed; none for private work
records.statutory_citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 42-158i, 42-158k, 42-158p and 42-158q (private work); § 49-41b (public work)
records.source_quote: No construction contract may provide for any retainage in an amount that exceeds five per cent of the estimated amount of a progress payment for the life of the construction project.

records.release_deadline: same time limits for payment of a payment request apply regardless of whether the payment request is for, or includes, retainage
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: a public entity may withhold from each progress payment made to the contractor an amount not exceeding 5 percent of the payment as retainage.

records.release_deadline: within 30 days after invoice at substantial completion
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: Retainage to a maximum of 5 percent of each progress payment. At the discretion of the owner and with the approval of the contractor, the retainage of each subcontractor may be released separately as the subcontractor completes his or her work.

records.release_deadline: not specified in this section
records.milestone_reduction: at 50% completion, retainage reduced to no more than 5%
records.source_quote: A construction contract may provide for the withholding of retainage of up to 10% of any payment made prior to the completion of 50% of the contract. When a contract is 50% complete, retainage withheld shall be reduced so that no more than 5% is held. After the contract is 50% complete, no more than 5% of the amount of any subsequent payments made under the contract may be held as retainage.

records.public_cap_pct: per contract terms (escrow required when withheld)
records.release_deadline: per contract terms
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: provision for retainage shall include in their respective contracts a provision that at the time any retainage is withheld, the state agency and/or contractor shall place such retainage in an escrow account, with a bank, savings and loan institution, or the State of Indiana or an instrumentality thereof, as escrow agent selected by mutual agreement

records.private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in this section
records.release_deadline: per section 573.14
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: The public corporation shall retain from each monthly payment not more than five percent of that amount which is determined to be due according to the estimate of the architect or engineer.

records.release_deadline: 30 days after substantial completion
records.milestone_reduction: retainage held after fifty-one percent (51%) of the construction project has been completed shall not be more than five percent (5%)
records.source_quote: until fifty percent (50%) of the construction project has been completed in accordance with the contract, a contracting entity, contractor, or subcontractor may withhold no more than ten percent (10%) retainage from the amount of any undisputed payment due, and retainage held after fifty-one percent (51%) of the construction project has been completed shall not be more than five percent (5%) of the total contract amount.

records.public_cap_pct: ten percent of the contract price on projects of less than five hundred thousand dollars, and five percent of the contract price on projects of five hundred thousand dollars or more
records.private_cap_pct: not stated in this Chapter, which governs public works; the Private Works Act provision formerly at R.S. 9:4814 was redesignated as R.S. 9:4856 by Acts 2019, No. 325 and legis.la.gov does not serve the redesignated text
records.release_deadline: until the expiration of forty-five days after the recordation of formal acceptance of such work, or notice of default by the contractor or subcontractor
records.escrow_required: no escrow is required; instead § 38:2249 is headed "Security in lieu of the amount withheld" and lets the contractor, with the written consent of his surety company, withdraw the entire retained amount by depositing security of equal value with the state treasurer or the treasurer of the public entity; the private-works escrow provisions are not served by legis.la.gov
records.milestone_reduction: none in this Section; the cap turns on the size of the project rather than on a completion milestone
records.statutory_citation: La. Rev. Stat. §§ 38:2248 and 38:2249; the Section may not be waived and does not apply to the Department of Transportation and Development
records.source_quote: A. No contracts for the construction, alteration, or repair of any public works executed in conformity with this Part shall provide that the state or any of its agencies, boards, or subdivisions or any other public entity letting such a contract may withhold payment of more than ten percent of the contract price on projects of less than five hundred thousand dollars, and five percent of the contract price on projects of five hundred thousand dollars or more until the expiration of forty-five days after the recordation of formal acceptance of such work, or notice of default by the contractor or subcontractor.

records.public_cap_pct: 5% of the total amount, where the contractor has furnished 100% payment security and 100% performance security (State procurement contracts)
records.private_cap_pct: 5% of the contract price, where the contractor has furnished 100% performance and payment security; the section does not apply to a contract under $100,000
records.release_deadline: within 90 days after the date of substantial completion
records.escrow_required: optional (public retainage may be deposited in an interest-bearing escrow account, and interest is then paid pro rata)
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.statutory_citation: Md. Code, Real Prop. § 9-304; Md. Code, State Fin. & Proc. § 13-225
records.source_quote: (e) Undisputed retention proceeds retained by an owner under this section shall be paid within 90 days after the date of substantial completion, as defined by the applicable contract or subcontract.

records.public_cap_pct: 5% of the approved amount of each periodic payment on public building contracts
records.private_cap_pct: 5% of any progress payment, on a contract for construction with an original contract price of not less than $3,000,000, excluding projects of 1 to 4 dwelling units
records.release_deadline: not later than 30 days following submission of the application
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.statutory_citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 149, § 29F; Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 30, § 39K
records.source_quote: (b) No contract for construction shall include retainage that exceeds 5 per cent of any progress payment.

records.public_cap_pct: Not more than 10% of the dollar value of all work in place until work is 50% in place
records.private_cap_pct: no statutory cap; Act 524 of 1980 reaches only a facility that is paid for with public funds or a special assessment
records.release_deadline: released to a contractor together with the final progress payment, which § 125.1562(3) times at thirty days after the architect or professional engineer certifies the work is in place, or fifteen days after the public agency receives the state or federal funds, whichever is later
records.escrow_required: public only (deposited in an interest bearing account in a regulated financial institution in this state, unless the retained funds are to come from a state or federal grant and have not yet been paid to the public agency)
records.milestone_reduction: After the work is 50% in place, additional retainage shall not be withheld unless the public agency determines that the contractor is not making satisfactory progress
records.statutory_citation: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 125.1561 to 125.1563 (Act 524 of 1980); § 125.1561(c) puts a contract worth less than $30,000.00, or one providing for 3 or fewer payments, outside "construction contract", and § 125.1561(h) puts the state transportation department, a school district, a junior or community college, the Michigan state housing development authority and a municipal electric utility outside "public agency"
records.source_quote: (1) To assure proper performance of a construction contract by the contractor, a public agency may retain a portion of each progress payment otherwise due as provided in this section.

records.release_deadline: 60 days after substantial completion
records.milestone_reduction: owner may reduce or eliminate retainage if work is progressing satisfactorily
records.source_quote: Retainage on a building and construction contract may not exceed five percent. An owner or owner's agent may reduce the amount of retainage and may eliminate retainage on any monthly contract payment if, in the owner's opinion, the work is progressing satisfactorily.

records.release_deadline: 30 days after acceptance and receipt of required documentation
records.milestone_reduction: public owner may reduce or eliminate retainage if work is proceeding satisfactorily
records.source_quote: Retainage withheld on any construction contract or subcontract for public works projects shall not exceed five percent of the value of the contract or subcontract.

records.public_cap_pct: 10% for a political subdivision; the Construction Prompt Pay Act does not reach State of Nebraska contracts
records.private_cap_pct: 10%, and no more than 5% of additional progress payments once the withheld scope is 50% complete
records.release_deadline: within forty-five days after the project, or a designated portion thereof, is substantially complete
records.milestone_reduction: at 50% complete, no more than five percent of any additional progress payment, conditional on assurances of continued performance and financial responsibility
records.source_quote: (1) For retainage, in an amount not to exceed the amount specified in the applicable contract, which shall not exceed a rate of ten percent. If the scope of work for the contractor or subcontractor from which retainage is withheld is fifty percent complete and if the contractor or subcontractor has performed work in accordance with the provisions in the applicable contract, no more than five percent of any additional progress payment may be withheld as retainage if the contractor or subcontractor provides or has provided satisfactory and reasonable assurances of continued performance and financial responsibility to complete the work;

records.release_deadline: within 30 days after occupancy, use, or recording of notice of completion, whichever occurs first
records.milestone_reduction: after 50% of the work has been completed, the public body may pay remaining progress payments without withholding additional retainage
records.source_quote: Ninety-five percent of the amount of any progress payment must be paid and 5 percent withheld as retainage until 50 percent of the work required by the contract has been performed.

records.public_cap_pct: 0% — the act repeals the retainage provisions of Chapter 57, Article 28 and prohibits the withholding of amounts due for work performed
records.private_cap_pct: 0% — the same prohibition binds a private owner, but the Prompt Payment Act does not apply to construction contracts for residential property containing four or fewer dwelling units
records.release_deadline: no retainage may be withheld, so there is nothing to release; an undisputed request for payment must be paid within twenty-one days after the owner receives it
records.escrow_required: no — the act prohibits withholding outright rather than regulating how retainage is held
records.milestone_reduction: none — withholding is prohibited from the first progress payment
records.statutory_citation: NMSA 1978 §§ 57-28-1 to 57-28-11 (Prompt Payment Act), as amended by Laws 2007, ch. 213 (S.B. 604, 2007 Regular Session); § 57-28-2 puts the department of transportation outside the act’s definition of "owner"
records.source_quote: RELATING TO TRADE PRACTICES; CHANGING THE NAME OF THE RETAINAGE ACT TO THE PROMPT PAYMENT ACT; ELIMINATING PROVISIONS OF CHAPTER 57, ARTICLE 28 NMSA 1978 CONCERNING RETAINAGE; PROHIBITING THE WITHHOLDING OF AMOUNTS DUE FOR WORK PERFORMED; AMENDING AND REPEALING SECTIONS OF THE NMSA 1978.

records.release_deadline: 30 days after final approval of the work
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: By mutual agreement of the relevant parties an owner may retain no more than five per centum of the contract sum as retainage. A contractor or subcontractor may also retain no more than five per centum for retainage and in no case shall retainage exceed the actual percentage retained by the owner. Retainage shall be released by the owner to the contractor no later than thirty days after the final approval of the work under a construction contract.

records.release_deadline: 60 days after substantial completion or beneficial occupancy
records.milestone_reduction: retainage eliminated after 50% complete with surety consent
records.source_quote: The owner shall not retain more than five percent (5%) of any periodic payment due a prime contractor.

records.release_deadline: governed by sections 153.13 and 153.14
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: Partial payments to the contractor for labor performed under either a unit or lump sum price contract shall be made at a rate of not less than ninety-six per cent of the estimates prepared by the contractor and approved by the architect or engineer.

records.release_deadline: interest commences 30 days after completion and acceptance
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: An owner, contractor or subcontractor may withhold as retainage an amount equal to not more than five percent of the contract price of the work completed.

records.release_deadline: 30 days after final acceptance of the work
records.milestone_reduction: contractor or subcontractor may post a maintenance bond for 120% of retainage upon reaching substantial completion to facilitate release
records.statutory_citation: 73 P.S. § 509 (Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act, Section 9)
records.source_quote: If payments under a construction contract are subject to retainage, any amounts which have been retained during the performance of the contract and which are due to be released to the contractor upon final completion shall be paid within 30 days after final acceptance of the work.

records.release_deadline: 21 days for owner to contractor; 7 days for contractor to subcontractor after receipt
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: Nothing in this chapter prevents the owner, the contractor, or a subcontractor from withholding application and certification for payment because of the following: unsatisfactory job progress, defective construction not remedied, disputed work, third party claims filed or reasonable evidence that claim will be filed, failure of contractor or subcontractor to make timely payments for labor, equipment, and materials, damage to owner, contractor, or another subcontractor, reasonable evidence that contract or subcontract cannot be completed for the unpaid balance of the contract or subcontract sum, or a reasonable amount for retainage.

records.release_deadline: 90 days after completion of the work or 90 days after substantial completion
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: (a) All construction contracts on any project in this state, both public and private, may provide for the withholding of retainage; provided, however, that the retainage amount may not exceed five percent (5%) of the amount of the contract.

records.release_deadline: upon completion of the work required to be performed under the contract
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: if the total value of a public works contract is less than $5 million, a governmental entity may not withhold retainage in an amount that exceeds 10 percent of the contract price and the rate of retainage may not exceed 10 percent for any item in a bid schedule or schedule of values for the project, including materials and equipment delivered on site to be installed;

records.release_deadline: included in the final payment
records.milestone_reduction: none
records.source_quote: the contractor shall be paid at least ninety-five percent of the earned sum when payment is due, with no more than five percent being retained to ensure faithful performance of the contract. All amounts withheld may be included in the final payment.

records.release_deadline: 60 days after completion of all contract work
records.milestone_reduction: contractor may request retainage be reduced to 100% of the value of work remaining
records.source_quote: public improvement contracts must provide, and public bodies must reserve, a contract retainage not to exceed five percent of the moneys earned by the contractor as a trust fund for the protection and payment of: (i) The claims of any person arising under the contract

records.public_cap_pct: 5% until 50% complete; 0% after 50% complete (unless unsatisfactory progress)
records.private_cap_pct: no statutory cap in this section
records.release_deadline: upon substantial completion
records.milestone_reduction: at 50% completion, no further retainage withheld (full payments resume)
records.source_quote: The retainage shall be an amount equal to not more than 5 percent of the estimate until 50 percent of the work has been completed. At 50 percent completion, further partial payments shall be made in full to the contractor and no additional amounts may be retained unless the architect or engineer certifies that the job is not proceeding satisfactorily, but amounts previously retained shall not be paid to the contractor.
